title: Council opposes Lancaster Street Highway 85 ramp closures
subtitle: Also: cemetery abandonment application, aquatics wage increases, and flood-mitigation land purchase on Borden Avenue South.
overview: Kitchener council heard a Region of Waterloo presentation on permanently closing the Highway 85 ramps at Lancaster Street, then voted to oppose the closure {{vote:m1}}. Council asked Regional Council not to support the environmental assessment and asked the Province and Region to consider signalizing the northbound off-ramp at Bridgeport Road. Regional staff cited safety, cycling links and capacity. Councillors raised concerns about traffic, trucks, local businesses and growth.

After a recess, council acted on three matters arising from a closed session. It directed the City Solicitor to seek a court order declaring the Kinzie (Kinsey) Biehn Pioneer (Memorial) Cemetery abandoned {{vote:m3}}. It approved higher wage rates for instructors, lifeguards and their head positions, effective May 1, 2023 {{vote:m4}}. It also approved acquiring properties at 170-188 Borden Avenue South and 59 Bedford Road, linked to the Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund {{vote:m5}}.
The Region was due to consider the ramp proposal the next day, so council's position goes to that body.

decisions.detail: Council opposed closing the Highway 85 ramps at Lancaster Street, asked the Region not to support the environmental assessment, and asked for signalization of the northbound off-ramp at Bridgeport Road {{vote:m1}}.
The City Solicitor was directed to apply to the Superior Court of Justice to declare the cemetery abandoned, and was authorized to start similar applications for other sites {{vote:m3}}.
Staff were directed to adjust wage rates for Instructor/Lifeguard and Head Instructor/Head Lifeguard positions, effective May 1, 2023 {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.item: Borden Avenue and Bedford Road land acquisition
decisions.detail: Council approved acquiring properties at 170-188 Borden Avenue South and 59 Bedford Road, and negotiating leases with existing tenants, under the Disaster Mitigation and Adaptation Fund {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Regional staff said the ramps contribute to collisions on southbound Highway 85, where the Ministry reports rates three to four times what is expected. They also said the ramps block a high-quality cycling route on Lancaster Street.

Councillors questioned the collision comparison with busier intersections elsewhere in the region. They also asked why this ramp was targeted after decades of service and noted municipalities usually ask the Province for more ramps, not fewer.

Councillors raised concerns about where truck traffic from nearby industrial businesses would go, added traffic at Bridgeport and Lancaster, and about planned new housing. Staff said extra travel time is about three minutes and no detailed business impact analysis was done.

A delegate for a nearby business opposed the closure, citing economic impact, cost, winter weather and light ramp use. The delegate suggested building cycling lanes first and deciding on closure later.

Some councillors said council had no chance to give input before the issue reached Regional Council. Another urged more effort to explain the benefits of cycling and reduce tension between drivers and cyclists.
